title: Jacobson radical descends through an integral overring
statement: Let B be a semilocal ring with Jacobson radical m_B, let B' be a semilocal ring integral over B [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], and let A be an intermediate ring B ⊆ A ⊆ B'. If the map Spec(B') to Spec(A) is surjective, then A is semilocal and its Jacobson radical m_A equals the radical of m_B A. Consequently, every element x of A that lies in the Jacobson radical of B' belongs to the radical of m_B A, so some power x^m belongs to m_B A.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09N2 proof, paragraph beginning 'Moreover, Spec(B') -> Spec(A) is surjective'

proof.text: The inclusions $B\subseteq A\subseteq B'$ are injective. Every element of $A$ is integral over $B$ because it lies in $B'$, and every element of $B'$ is integral over $A$ because its monic equation over $B$ is also an equation over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure].

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09N2 proof, intermediate ring $B\subset A\subset B'$; integrality by Algebra Definition 00GI

proof.text: For each maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ of $A$, the assumed surjectivity of $\operatorname{Spec}(B')\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ supplies a prime $\mathfrak q$ of $B'$ above it. As $B'$ is integral over $A$ (step 1), [lem-weil-pbc-integral-prime-over-maximal-maximal] makes $\mathfrak q$ maximal. Conversely the contraction to $A$ of any maximal ideal of $B'$ is maximal by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-algebra-ideal-in-radical]. Hence the maximal ideals of $A$ are exactly the contractions of maximal ideals of $B'$, a finite set since $B'$ is semilocal. Thus $A$ is semilocal.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09N2 proof, sentence beginning 'Moreover, Spec(B') -> Spec(A) is surjective'

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-algebra-ideal-in-radical] to the integral extension $B\subseteq A$ from step 1 and $I=\mathfrak m_B$ to get $\mathfrak m_BA\subseteq\mathfrak m_A$. The Jacobson radical is an intersection of maximal ideals and hence is radical, so $\sqrt{\mathfrak m_BA}\subseteq\mathfrak m_A$. For the reverse inclusion, let $\mathfrak p$ be any prime of $A$ containing $\mathfrak m_BA$. Its contraction $\mathfrak r$ to $B$ contains $\mathfrak m_B=\bigcap_{i=1}^t\mathfrak m_i$, where the $\mathfrak m_i$ are the finitely many maximal ideals of $B$. The product $\prod_i\mathfrak m_i$ lies in that intersection, so primality of $\mathfrak r$ implies $\mathfrak m_i\subseteq\mathfrak r$ for some $i$; maximality gives $\mathfrak r=\mathfrak m_i$. Now [lem-weil-pbc-integral-prime-over-maximal-maximal] for $B\subseteq A$ makes $\mathfrak p$ maximal. Therefore every prime containing $\mathfrak m_BA$ contains $\mathfrak m_A$, so $\mathfrak m_A\subseteq\sqrt{\mathfrak m_BA}$, proving equality. For $t=0$, the empty intersection is $B$, whence $\mathfrak m_BA=A$ and both sides are the unit ideal.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09N2 proof, sentence 'Note that $\mathfrak m_A = \sqrt{\mathfrak m_B A}$'; finite-intersection argument supplied

proof.text: Let $x\in A\cap\mathfrak m_{B'}$. For every maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ of $A$, step 2 provides a maximal ideal $\mathfrak q$ of $B'$ contracting to $\mathfrak n$. Since $x\in\mathfrak m_{B'}$, it lies in $\mathfrak q$, so its contraction lies in $\mathfrak n$. Thus $x\in\mathfrak m_A=\sqrt{\mathfrak m_BA}$ by step 3. By the definition of radical, $x^m\in\mathfrak m_BA$ for some integer $m>0$.
